text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose 2.08% today after falling sharply yesterday, recovering some ground as oil-market uncertainty eased. The main driver appears to be relief around Iran tensions: yesterday oil prices fell over 3% after the U.S. signaled it would use economic pressure rather than military strikes, but today's reports suggest Iran and Oman are moving toward a deal on safe shipping through the Strait of Hormuz—a critical chokepoint for global oil supply. When geopolitical risk to oil flows decreases, refiner stocks often bounce back because refiners profit when they can reliably source crude.

The broader pattern here reflects how refining companies are caught between competing forces: war risk premiums tend to boost oil prices (which can squeeze refiner margins), while resolution of supply-chain threats can calm the market and sometimes ease margins in the other direction. The 2-week gain of 4% suggests investors have been rotating into energy plays amid this geopolitical turbulence, with yesterday's dip now partially reversed.
